title: HelperSSHForwardClosedEvent
description: The announcement that a listener is over: the coordinator asked (its own unforward), the far side's connection died under it, or the server closed it. It exists for the case nothing else covers — a caller parked in Accept, which would otherwise wait for ever — and the CAUSE is the field that separates the two meanings: empty when the coordinator itself asked, the helper's sentence when nobody here did. It is announced on both ways of ending, for the reason a channel's close is: an id the coordinator has already forgotten is dropped by its own routing, and one dropped frame is cheaper than a reader waiting for an end that never comes.

forward.description: The listener that ended, as 32 hex characters.

error.description: The helper's own sentence for an end nobody here asked for: the far side's connection dying under the listener is the case a -R forward and the remote lifecycle channel both have to hear, because both hold an Accept. Empty when the coordinator's own unforward is what ended it.
